sentence: This project builds imaging tools that measure how the healthy and diseased human brain uses energy, using a clinical MRI scanner.
This project studies the neural circuits that explain why some people cannot stop taking prescription opioids despite aversive life consequences.
This project studies how T cells interact with myeloid cells to fight lung cancer and builds a model that predicts outcomes for patients.
This project provides instruments and expertise for imaging at high spatial and temporal resolution so researchers can do experiments that are not possible in their own laboratories.
This project compares dedicated breast CT with digital breast tomosynthesis to find out whether breast CT could work for breast cancer screening.
This project studies how glycosylated RNAs from neutrophils interact with a receptor on endothelial cells to help neutrophils get recruited.
This project uses genetic testing results linked to cancer registry records to find out whether their management fits each patient and whether cancer mortality varies by result.
This project studies which features of protein and RNA molecules control how biomolecular condensates form inside cells, using simulation and machine-learning methods.
This project uses a mouse model to study how neuromelanin in dopaminergic neurons relates to Parkinson's disease.
This project studies why cervical cancer comes back after chemoradiation therapy and tests whether genomic tests can detect recurrence.
This project studies how cyclic GMP binds claudin-5 mRNA to strengthen the blood-brain barrier in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease and aging.
This project uses specialized methods to find unconventional targets on melanoma cells that cytotoxic T cells could recognize.
This project studies how apoptosis and necroptosis, two pathways of cell death, are regulated, and looks for potential drug candidates.
This project advances a technology so that protein dynamics and transitions between conformational states can be studied.
This project uses single-cell analysis to study how hematopoietic stem cells change with aging at the molecular level.
This project designs optoelectroactive citrate biocomposites and studies how they promote bone repair.
This project provides next generation sequencing services that support cancer research, including single cell transcriptomics and spatial transcriptomics.
This project uses mixed methods to study what drives suicidal thoughts and behaviors among rural sexual minority adults.
This project provides data management, database and statistical support for a research program on networks in aging.
This project studies how a neuropeptide receptor controls melanoma development and metastases through interactions between neurons and pericytes.
